feed.title: Game Development — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome Babylon.js
entry.summary: A resource list for Babylon.js, a 3D game engine for web and native.

entry.title: Awesome Flame
entry.summary: A resource list for Flame, the game engine for Flutter.

entry.title: Awesome Game Boy Dev
entry.summary: Game development for the Game Boy — assemblers, tools and hardware docs. Unlike modern engine lists it focuses on programming constrained retro hardware.

entry.title: Awesome Game Development
entry.summary: A resource list covering every branch of game development from engines to asset tools. Unlike engine-specific lists it is engine-agnostic — a broad starting map.

entry.title: Awesome Game Engine Dev
entry.summary: Resources for writing the game engine itself, not a game — rendering, physics, ECS. Unlike engine-usage lists it aims at building an engine from scratch.

entry.title: Awesome Game Remakes
entry.summary: A list of actively maintained, open-source remakes of classic games. Unlike emulators the game’s engine has been rewritten from scratch — the code is readable.

entry.title: Awesome Games of Coding
entry.summary: A list of games that teach a programming language by making games. Unlike dry exercises it ties learning to a game’s progression.

entry.title: Awesome Godot
entry.summary: A list of plugins, tutorials and example projects for the open-source Godot engine. Unlike the official docs it gathers the tools and templates the community produced.

entry.title: Awesome Learn Gamedev
entry.summary: Course, book and community resources for learning to make games. Unlike tool lists it offers an ordered path and also covers side crafts like art, audio and design.

entry.title: Awesome libGDX
entry.summary: A list of libraries and resources for libGDX, the Java game framework.

entry.title: Awesome LÖVE2D
entry.summary: A list of resources and libraries for LÖVE, the Lua-based game engine.

entry.title: Awesome Minecraft
entry.summary: A list gathering Minecraft servers, mods and tools.

entry.title: Awesome Open Source Games
entry.summary: A list of playable games whose source is open. Unlike game stores these are projects whose code you can read to learn how they were made and build on.

entry.title: Awesome OpenGL
entry.summary: A list of libraries and tutorials for OpenGL, the 2D/3D rendering API.

entry.title: Awesome PICO-8
entry.summary: A list of games and tools for PICO-8, the retro-constrained fantasy console.

entry.title: Awesome Vulkan
entry.summary: A resource list for Vulkan, the low-overhead 3D graphics and compute API.

entry.title: MagicTools
entry.summary: A list of tools and resources for game and graphics development — sprites, tiles, audio, level editors. Unlike engine lists it focuses on the helper tools in the production pipeline.

entry.title: CodinGame
entry.summary: A platform that has you solve programming puzzles with a game theme, showing your code’s result in a game scene. Unlike dry problem sets it animates your solution visually.

entry.title: Game Programming Patterns
entry.summary: Robert Nystrom’s free book on the design patterns that recur in game code. Unlike general design-pattern books its examples are specific to the game loop and performance.

entry.title: Unity
entry.summary: The most widely used cross-platform game engine; 2D/3D, mobile and console. Unlike Godot it has a huge asset store and industry ubiquity — most job listings ask for it.
